web-mobile.connects.appGone: This app is no longer on this station: it may have connected already, or been removed.
web-mobile.connects.avatarNote: Pick one below, or upload an image.
web-mobile.connects.config.step1: Open {link} and sign in with an account in the Slack workspace the bot will live in.
web-mobile.connects.config.step2: Scroll to "Your App Configuration Tokens" at the bottom, click Generate Token and choose this workspace.
web-mobile.connects.config.step3: Paste the Refresh Token starting with xoxe-1- below. {name} renews it itself, so you won't need to again.
web-mobile.connects.configNote: With a Slack configuration token, {name} creates the app in Slack for you: set the name, avatar and permissions here instead of configuring each in Slack's admin pages. It's used only for you.
web-mobile.connects.deleteText: The Slack connection will close. You'll need to delete the app in Slack yourself.

web-mobile.connects.deleteTextSessions.one: The Slack connection will close; its 1 session's history is kept but won't receive messages. You'll need to delete the app in Slack yourself.
web-mobile.connects.deleteTextSessions.other: The Slack connection will close; its {n} sessions' history is kept but they won't receive messages. You'll need to delete the app in Slack yourself.

web-mobile.connects.disabled: Disabled; the Slack connection is closed
web-mobile.connects.dropText: Removes it from {name} only. The app stays in Slack; delete it on Slack's app settings page if you no longer need it.
web-mobile.connects.everyMessage: Every message it can see goes into the session.
web-mobile.connects.install.manual: The app is ready. {link}, then copy the Bot User OAuth Token (starts with xoxb-) from the {oauth}.
web-mobile.connects.install.oauth: The app is ready. {link}: click "Allow" in Slack and the bot token goes to the station automatically.
web-mobile.connects.install.socket: Generate an App-Level Token on the {link} page and copy it (starts with xapp-; scopes are preselected).
web-mobile.connects.manual.create: Create an app in Slack with {name}'s configuration
web-mobile.connects.manual.install: Install it to the workspace on the Install App page and copy the Bot User OAuth Token.
web-mobile.connects.manual.socket: Generate an App-Level Token on the app's Socket Mode page (scopes are preselected).
web-mobile.connects.manualLong: Create the app in Slack yourself, without a configuration token
web-mobile.connects.manualShort: Create the app yourself, without a configuration token
web-mobile.connects.mentionOff: Every message it can see in the channel goes into the session.
web-mobile.connects.mentionOn: Later replies in a thread it was @mentioned in don't need another @.
web-mobile.connects.noModels: No models are enabled in {runtime} profiles yet. Enable some in the profiles on the station page first.
web-mobile.connects.noModelsHere: No models are enabled in this station's profiles yet. Enable some in the profiles on the station page first.
web-mobile.connects.noSession: No session yet; the next message starts one.
web-mobile.connects.noSessions: No sessions yet. @{name} in Slack to start one.
web-mobile.connects.noTokens: This connect isn't linked to Slack yet.
web-mobile.connects.none: No connects on this machine yet
web-mobile.connects.note: A connect is where people reach {name}, such as a Slack app. Each connect lives on one station and is bound to a model.
web-mobile.connects.offlineList: Station offline; can't read its connects
web-mobile.connects.offlineWait: Station offline. Continue once it's back
web-mobile.connects.ownerNote: The owner decides whose "Added by me" list it appears in.
web-mobile.connects.pickSessionNote: From now on, messages to "{name}" go to the chosen session. The old session is kept but gets no new messages from this connect.
web-mobile.connects.pickTeam: Which Slack workspace's configuration token to create the app with.
web-mobile.connects.profileFirstNote: A connect needs a profile to run models. Add one, then come back to add the connect.
web-mobile.connects.runNote: New sessions use the new settings; ongoing ones keep those they started with.
web-mobile.connects.runSaved: Saved. New sessions will use the new settings
web-mobile.connects.runtimeNote: Runs on {runtime}, which can't be changed after creation; for another runtime, create a new connect. Ongoing sessions keep the settings they started with.
web-mobile.connects.scopesNote: Uses the default permissions (all on); you can change them on a computer later.
web-mobile.connects.sessionPlaceholder: Name it (optional), for example: On call
web-mobile.connects.tokensNote: You can change just one; leave the other empty to keep the saved one.

web-mobile.profiles.codexNote: On the OpenAI page that opens, sign in with the ChatGPT account {name} should use and paste the code. This continues on its own when done. If the page says device code sign-in is off, turn it on in ChatGPT's security settings first.
web-mobile.profiles.copyCodeFailed: Couldn't copy the code. Copy it from above by hand
web-mobile.profiles.copyOpen: Copy code and open sign-in page
web-mobile.profiles.deleteText: Removes it from {name}'s configuration only; the config directory and the sign-in in it are kept.
web-mobile.profiles.disableText: {name} stops using this sign-in on the machine. The sign-in itself is unaffected and can be used again later.
web-mobile.profiles.envNote: The runtime starts with these variables to reach your model service. {route} in a value is replaced with the session's route ID.
web-mobile.profiles.fastNote: Used by sessions that follow the plan; Fast uses more quota or credits
web-mobile.profiles.loginDone: Signed in. To switch accounts, sign in again.
web-mobile.profiles.loginWhere: The sign-in happens on the machine running {name}; you only authorize it in the browser.
web-mobile.profiles.loginWhereAdd: The sign-in happens on the machine running {name}; you only authorize it in the browser. The profile is added once the sign-in succeeds.
web-mobile.profiles.machineLogins: Already signed in on this machine
web-mobile.profiles.machineNote: "Use this account" uses this machine's own sign-in, so switching accounts or signing out on the machine changes it too. Sign-ins the station can't read (Codex's in the keychain, or a locked keychain) can't be used directly; sign in once separately for {name}, and the original sign-in is unaffected.
web-mobile.profiles.manualLogin: You can also sign in manually on that machine
web-mobile.profiles.modelsEmpty: After the profile is checked, the models it can use are listed here. Tick them to use them.

web-mobile.profiles.none: No profiles on this machine yet
